solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Region needs detective, rigorous

parts.note: DI is the abbreviation for Detective Inspector
rigorous means strict

explanation.surface: An area of policing demands a detective who is thorough and strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or region marked out for administrative purposes.

clue.text: County firm upset staff at first

indicators.note: says the overturned staff stands at the front, before the word for firm
in a down clue, upset means the word for staff is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a staff is a rod or pole
firm means set, as a jelly sets hard

explanation.surface: A rural business turns its workforce upside down, starting with the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a rod; 'upset' turns ROD into DOR. DORSET is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is one of the shire counties of southern England, an example of a county.

clue.text: Nationalist in elaborate salute in Brunei, say

indicators.note: the short word for nationalist is placed in the middle of the reworked salute letters
an elaborate version is worked up and rearranged, so the letters of salute are shuffled

explanation.surface: A patriot offers a showy salute during a visit to Brunei.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' reorders the six letters of the salute; 'in' places the short nationalist inside that jumble, near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is ruled by a sultan, so it is an example of a sultanate, with 'say' flagging the example.

clue.text: Rather loyal ball arranged here?

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather patriotic dance might well be organised in this grand venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the London concert venue hosts grand, patriotic events such as the Last Night of the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous domed London concert hall, a fitting place to stage a patriotic, royal-flavoured ball.

clue.text: After church find more appropriate section of book

indicators.note: the word for more appropriate comes after the abbreviation for church

parts.note: apt means appropriate, so apter is more appropriate

explanation.surface: Following a church service, one finds a more suitable passage to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Books are divided into numbered parts, each called by this name.

clue.text: Objective: make deserter return — understand?

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the word for deserter is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: An officer asks whether the aim is to make a runaway soldier come back.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is an aim or goal, something you set out to hit.

clue.text: Legislation redrafted often — claim a part

indicators.note: redrafted means written out again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A law rewritten many times might lay claim to some portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by the UK Parliament is a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Good contest for cricketing great

parts.note: a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A fine match is put on to honour a legend of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: W G Grace was a famous Victorian English cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: W G Grace, the bearded Victorian batsman, is among cricket's most famous players.

clue.text: More fashionable guy making effort without limit

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for one making an effort goes around the word for limit

parts.note: a trier is someone who tries hard
an end is a limit

explanation.surface: A fellow strives endlessly to be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without limit' looks like 'endlessly', but 'without' is the old sense of outside: the striver's word wraps the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, so trendier is the comparative, more fashionable.

clue.text: Gathering, our group will prosper

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering
we'll is short for we will, our group being we

explanation.surface: A team predicts its own success at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of WE'LL drops out in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To do well is an idiom for to thrive or succeed, the same as prosper.

clue.text: Recovery in market? Missing the point, really

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter is dropped from really

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a speaker has failed to grasp what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing the point' sounds like a criticism, but 'point' is the compass point E.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a rise in share prices after a fall, a market recovery.

clue.text: A fight at fancy café leading to reversal

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing

indicators.note: fancy here means fancifully remade, so the letters of café are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brawl at a smart coffee shop leads to things turning around.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a complete change of direction or opinion, a turnaround.

clue.text: Ornamental wear of English saint, essentially better

parts.note: Paul is a saint, the apostle

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the inner letters of better are taken

explanation.surface: An English saint's decorative clothing is, at heart, superior.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is a decorative shoulder piece on a uniform, a piece of ornamental dress.

clue.text: Associate avoiding right enthusiast

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so the letter for right is left out

parts.note: a friend is an associate or companion

explanation.surface: A companion keeps away from a keen fan of the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend can mean an addict or fanatic, as in a fresh-air fiend.

clue.text: US writer, one posting letters

definitions.meaning: someone who sends things by mail

explanation.surface: An American author is also a person dropping letters into a postbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was a US novelist, and literally this is someone who sends post.

clue.text: Unwelcome flow in field for example a king recalled

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters for example, a and king are read backwards

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A meadow where a king was summoned back suffers a damaging seepage.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is an escape of fluid, an unwanted outflow.

clue.text: Detest couple claiming home after sailor (old)

indicators.note: the word for couple follows the sailor and the old marker

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the word for couple surrounds the word for home

parts.note: to mate is to couple or pair
in means at home

explanation.surface: A pair hates a home following on from a seaman of former days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claiming' means the word for couple holds the word for home inside itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe intensely, a strong synonym of detest.

clue.text: Following whisky, maybe, journalist full of energy

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the journalist goes after the drink

parts.note: whisky is an example of a spirit, with maybe flagging the example
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: After a dram or two, a reporter is full of vim.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means lively and energetic, full of verve.

clue.text: Lineswoman?

parts.note: not a tennis or football official but a woman who writes lines of verse

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a female line judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A lineswoman suggests sport; the lines here are lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A female writer of verse, someone whose craft is producing lines of poetry.

clue.text: Tool in second ramshackle dwelling

parts.note: a hovel is a squalid, tumbledown house

explanation.surface: An implement is kept in a run-down second home.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a digging implement, a garden tool.

clue.text: Inform about Swiss crossbow expert never coming back

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple from his son's head

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word for never is read backwards

parts.note: no as in no way, never

explanation.surface: Someone reports on the Swiss archer who never returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell on someone is to report them, an idiom for informing against.

clue.text: Girl in that place with appeal

parts.note: there means in that place
SA, sex appeal, is appeal

explanation.surface: A young woman over yonder has charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female first name, so stands for a girl.

clue.text: Not used to northern scientist

parts.note: something new has not been used before

explanation.surface: A researcher is unaccustomed to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not used to' reads as one phrase meaning unaccustomed, but the split falls after 'used'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton, the English physicist, is one of the most famous scientists.

clue.text: Disprove objection after teaching of religion

indicators.note: the word for objection comes after the school subject

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A protest raised after a scripture lesson proves it false.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute an argument, showing it is false.

clue.text: Salty bacon (rasher) is nettling you initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the over-salted bacon is irritating them.
explanation.definitionFit: Briny means tasting of brine, salt water, so it is salty.

clue.text: Love new private eastern worker

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of private are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh soldier from the East is besotted with his job.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a skilled factory hand.

clue.text: Cheers current decreases applied to energy for islanders

indicators.note: applied to means attached to, so the earlier pieces are fixed in front of the energy letter

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
I is the symbol for electric current
wanes means decreases
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A thank-you as the power supply drops off is given to the energy firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Taiwan, the island off China's coast, are islanders.

clue.text: Index actually not fully correct

indicators.note: not fully means only part of the words is used, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A reference list is, in truth, not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise and accurate, so correct.

clue.text: Oddly mistaken about article: "Born yesterday"?

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the article
mistaken means got wrong, so the letters of oddly are jumbled

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece oddly gets wrong a claim that someone is naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born yesterday' usually means naive; taken literally it means one day old. 'mistaken' makes DYOLD from ODDLY, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature born yesterday is literally one day old, the question mark flagging the literal reading.

clue.text: Long fellow as member of distinguished group

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
he is a male, a fellow
on as in on the committee, being a member

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to join an elite circle as one of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a set of the most revered or famous figures in a field.
